instructions: These sketches describe activity types, not specific venues — they work for any city. Present in groups of 4 during onboarding. After collecting reactions, run the inference algorithm in SKILL.md to derive preferences.

sketches.sketch: Renting bikes and riding a waterfront or trail route — an hour or two of moving around, then food somewhere casual at the end
A touring Broadway show or major performing arts event at a historic theater — pre-show dinner before curtain
An afternoon at a major art museum, then wandering a walkable indie neighborhood — coffee, maybe a bookstore, dinner at whatever looks good
An outdoor summer concert or festival — live music, open air, a crowd that's all in a good mood
A long walk through a well-known local park — no agenda, good conversation, coffee from somewhere nearby
A professional sports game — local team, downtown arena or stadium, fun even if you don't follow the sport closely
A nature preserve or hiking trail — quiet, maybe wildlife or good views, genuinely away from the city for a few hours
Dinner at a unique architectural or historically interesting venue — a repurposed building, a rooftop, somewhere with a story behind it
A full day eating your way through city neighborhoods — market or brunch in the morning, local spots through the afternoon, proper dinner at night
A day trip to a major natural attraction within an hour or two — somewhere dramatic that you don't need to live near to appreciate
A show at a small local music venue — a band you've never heard of or a known touring act, standing room, out by midnight
A slow neighborhood afternoon — good coffee, an independent bookstore, window shopping, stopping for dinner whenever you get hungry
